sets:
Review the statements below.

I. Primary markets are for new issues.
II. Secondary markets trade existing securities.

What is the PRIMARY role of the bond rating agencies?

Review the claims below. Which combination is correct?

I. Help to guarantee the repayment of bond issuers by assuring investors they will be paid back.
II. Assess the ability of the bond issuers to meet their obligations and assign a default risk rating to the bonds.
III. Fix the coupon rate of the bond rated by them.
IV. Act as underwriters to the bonds rated by them.

Statement II is true. The textbook states rating agencies 'assess the ability of the bond issuers to meet their obligations and assign a default risk rating to the bonds'. They do NOT guarantee repayment, fix coupon rates, or underwrite bonds.

Review the statements below in relation to secrecy and permitted disclosure under the financial services framework.

I. Information may be disclosed where written permission from the relevant account holder has been obtained.
II. Information may be disclosed where required for criminal or civil proceedings.
III. Internal management approval alone is enough to override secrecy even where no legal basis, permission or recognised exception exists.
IV. Secrecy duties end automatically when employment ends and no further confidentiality obligation remains.
I and II only — both statements identify recognised situations where disclosure may be permitted under the secrecy framework
I and III only — internal approval is sufficient to replace statutory permitted disclosure requirements
II and IV only — proceedings matter, but secrecy obligations end once employment ends
III and IV only — both statements treat secrecy as an internal policy rather than a statutory obligation
Statements I and II are correct. Secrecy duties continue after employment, and disclosure must fall within a permitted ground.
A principal-protected structured product invests RM200,000 and gives 50% participation in a 8% rise of the underlying asset. Ignoring fees and taxes, what amount is payable at maturity?
Payoff = principal + principal × underlying return × participation. = RM200,000 + RM200,000 × 8% × 50% = RM208,000.

Review the statements below.

I. Exchange-traded markets normally have clearer oversight.
II. OTC contracts are usually privately negotiated.
III. OTC markets always use a central exchange as counterparty.
IV. Primary markets trade only previously issued securities.
Statements I and II are correct.

Which of the following on options is CORRECT?

From an investor-protection perspective, which statements are true?

I. American options only allow the buyer to exercise the option on expiry date.
II. An option is a financial instrument that grants the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell specified underlying assets at a specified exercise price on or before a specified date.
III. European option grants the buyer the right to exercise at any time on or before expiry date.
IV. A put option allows a buyer the right to buy a specified underlying asset at a specified price on or before a specified date.

Statement II is true. The textbook defines an option as 'a financial instrument that gives the holder the right (but not the obligation) to buy or sell a specified asset at a specified price on or before a specified date'. American options can be exercised anytime before expiry; European options only on expiry date. A put option gives the right to SELL, not buy.

Syarikat ABC is a money and FX broker. Which of the following in relation to Syarikat ABC is TRUE?

Which combination gives the best answer?

I. Syarikat ABC is registered with Companies Commission of Malaysia and thus is not regulated by BNM.
II. Syarikat ABC may provide investment recommendations to market participants as part of its services.
III. Syarikat ABC matches buyer and seller of money and foreign exchange market products and charges a fee or commission in the process.
IV. Syarikat ABC may sometimes offer non-public information to solicit business from market participants.

Statement III is true. The textbook states brokers 'act as intermediaries between buyers and sellers' and charge 'a fee or commission'. Brokers regulated by BNM must comply with BNM guidelines regardless of their Companies Commission registration. Brokers do not give investment recommendations (that is a dealer/advisor function) and must not share non-public information.

During an exam-style client discussion, a relationship manager is asked to identify the most accurate regulatory or product-treatment statement before making any recommendation. which one of the following financial instruments is considered a money market instrument?
A 6-month commercial paper issued by a corporate.
A 3-year NID issued by an investment bank.

The money market involves 'short-term borrowing and lending via assets or securities with original maturities of up to one (1) year'. A 6-month commercial paper qualifies. A 3-year MGS, 10-year zero coupon bond, and 3-year NID are all long-term instruments (above 1 year maturity).
A primary market is mainly used for:
Primary markets are used for new securities issuance.

Under Section 19 of AMLA, RIs are required to designate a compliance officer at the management level to oversee the implementation of a compliance programme. What is a KEY role of the compliance officer?

Assess the statements below and select the correct combination.

I. To manage the RIs' marketing and onboarding of customers at the respective branch or subsidiary.
II. To oversee the proper implementation of internal programme on AMLA and report suspicious transactions.
III. To personally approve high-value transactions of certain limits.
IV. To conduct study on competitor's compliance programme.

Statement II is true. The compliance officer's key role under Section 19 is to oversee 'proper maintenance of records' and 'reporting of suspicious transactions', and to apply internal AML programmes. They do not personally approve transactions or study competitors.

Which answer reflects the correct investor-protection outcome?

Financial institutions should not recommend products to customers unless they are reasonably satisfied that the product meets the particular needs of the customers.

Which of the following procedures will satisfy the above concerns?

Customer suitability procedures are the process through which financial institutions ensure that products recommended are appropriate for a customer's needs, risk profile, and financial situation. This is the key requirement of KYC under the CMSA and Guidelines on Investor Protection.

7-year fixed income securities with 5% coupon priced at par when market interest rates are at 5%. One (1) year later, the yield curve moves upward by 100 basis points across all maturities. What will happen to the bond?

Review the claims below. Which combination is correct?

I. Bond price will rise above par as its coupon is now below the market interest rate.
II. Bond price will remain unchanged as the maturity of the bond is shorter by one (1) year.
III. Investors will put back the bond to the issuer since the yield curve has shifted upwards.
IV. Bond price will fall below par as its coupon is now lower than the market interest rate.

Statement IV is true. When yields rise by 100 bps, the discount rate applied to future cash flows increases, reducing the present value of all cash flows. The textbook's price-yield curve shows that higher yields result in lower bond prices. A bond with a 5% coupon and 6% market rate will trade at a discount.
An option has intrinsic value of RM0.50 and time value of RM0.25. What is the option premium?
Option premium = intrinsic value + time value = RM0.50 + RM0.25 = RM0.75.

Under the Guidelines on AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs, which of the following is a CDD requirement for corporate customers?

I. RIs are required to verify the registration number of the company only.
II. RIs are required to identify beneficial owners and understand the control structure of the company.
III. RIs to check only the name and address for a listed company with the exchange.
IV. RIs are required to identify the identity of shareholders for a public listed company in Bursa Malaysia.

Statement II is true. For corporate customers, RIs must 'identify the beneficial owner and take reasonable measures to verify the identity of the beneficial owner' and understand the control structure of the company. Verifying only the registration number or name/address is insufficient.

A Hong Kong tech firm wants to borrow RM20 million from a Licensed Onshore Bank (LOB) to lease equipment from a Malaysian supplier. Which of the following is consistent with BNM's rules that govern this transaction?

I. The Ringgit borrowing has to be approved by BNM because it is a non-resident company.
II. The Ringgit borrowing by non-residents from an LOB is capped at RM10 million only.
III. The Hong Kong tech firm can borrow any amount for real-sector activities, provided the lender is an LOB.
IV. The Hong Kong tech firm must convert the loan to USD if the equipment is exported.

Statement III is true. Under BNM's FEA rules, non-residents (including foreign firms) are free to borrow Ringgit from Licensed Onshore Banks (LOBs) for real-sector activities without a specified cap. No BNM prior approval is needed for real-sector Ringgit borrowing from an LOB.

During a detailed client suitability and investor-protection discussion, a relationship manager must identify the single best answer using the product features, regulatory duty and client-treatment principles in the study text. which one of the following bonds has the highest default risk?
A zero coupon bond issued by a corporation.
A high-yield bond rated D by RAM.

A bond rated D by RAM 'is either currently in default or faces imminent default on its financial obligations'. BNM notes are government securities with essentially zero default risk; Cagamas bonds are quasi-government. A corporate zero coupon bond carries credit risk but is investment grade. The D-rated bond has the highest default risk.
An arbitrager mainly seeks to profit from:
Arbitragers seek pricing discrepancies across markets.

If a bond is trading at a premium to its par value, what does it most likely imply?

Which statements should remain in the client explanation?

I. Bond has a high coupon rate.
II. Market interest rate is lower than the coupon of the bond.
III. Market interest rate is higher than the coupon of the bond.
IV. Issuer is about to redeem the bond before maturity.

Statement II is true. When a bond trades at a premium (price > par), the bond's coupon rate is higher than the prevailing market interest rate, making the bond more attractive. Buyers are willing to pay more than par to obtain the above-market coupon payments. This is the direct result of the inverse price-yield relationship.

Before any product selection is made, suitability work should consider objectives, financial situation, particular needs, experience, time horizon, liquidity needs and risk tolerance. The process is not simply a formality because it helps ensure that the proposed product is appropriate and that any recommendation has a proper basis. This process is best described as:
KYC and suitability assessment support financial needs analysis and reasonable-basis recommendations.

Which option avoids the common exam trap?

Select the option that descriptions CORRECTLY reflects the character of different market structures?
Participants in an exchange traded market clear their transactions through a centralised clearing house.
OTC transactions are where the buyers and sellers face each other through an intermediary such as an exchange.
FX transactions are based on standardised amounts conducted through an organised exchange.
Exchange traded market has less liquidity compared to OTC market.

In an exchange-traded market, 'the central clearing house of the exchange becomes sellers to the buyers and buyers to the sellers' — the clearing house interposes itself as the counterparty to every trade. OTC is where 'buyers face sellers directly without an intermediary such as an exchange'. The exchange-traded market also has greater, not lesser, regulatory oversight, and OTC typically has less liquidity than the exchange.
A comparison between two products is required. What is the best conduct response?
Good conduct requires objective comparison and avoidance of misrepresentation.

What should be done or concluded based on the scenario?

During a detailed client suitability and investor-protection discussion, a relationship manager must identify the single best answer using the product features, regulatory duty and client-treatment principles in the study text. which of the following structured products' delivery formats is mostly used by investment banks?

The textbook states commercial banks 'normally issue FRNID, NID, NID-i and SP (structured products)'. For investment banks, structured notes are the primary delivery format used to issue principal and non-principal protected structured products to investors.
A call option has an exercise price of RM105. The underlying asset is currently RM120. What is the intrinsic value of the call option?
Call intrinsic value = max(spot price − exercise price, 0). = max(RM120 − RM105, 0) = RM15.
A bank officer is asked to disclose a customer’s account information. Under Section 134 of the Financial Services Act 2013, which circumstance is MOST clearly a permitted disclosure?
A colleague verbally says the customer will probably agree.
The relationship manager believes disclosure will improve sales conversion.
The customer gives written permission for the disclosure.
The customer is a high-net-worth client of the bank.
Permitted disclosure includes written consent from the customer or legal representative. Verbal assumptions, sales convenience, or customer wealth status are not sufficient.

Review the statements below.

I. Section 92 requires reasonable basis.
II. Misleading information is a conduct concern.

During a detailed client suitability and investor-protection discussion, a relationship manager must identify the single best answer using the product features, regulatory duty and client-treatment principles in the study text. which of the following deposits or financial products is insured by PIDM?
A structured product issued by an Islamic bank.
A joint deposit account placed with an investment bank.
A business deposit placed with the commercial bank.
A USD deposit placed with a commercial bank in Singapore.

PIDM protects deposits placed with commercial banks and Islamic banks that are PIDM member institutions. Business deposits placed with commercial banks are eligible. Investment banks are not PIDM member institutions. Structured products and deposits placed overseas (Singapore) are not covered. Foreign currency deposits at Malaysian member banks ARE covered.

Abu works as a Relationship Manager in a financial banking group with businesses including banking, insurance, and takaful operations. One of his main responsibilities is to explain and disclose to new customers the financial products that are protected by PIDM.

Which of the following statements Abu made to his customers complies with PIDM mandates?
All financial products offered by the financial banking group are protected by PIDM as the financial banking group is a member bank of PIDM.
The financial banking group is licensed and regulated by BNM and subject to stringent regulatory requirements, and thus, BNM will protect the financial banking group from bankruptcy.
The maximum limit of coverage is RM250,000 per depositor per member bank, and the maximum limit of protection is RM500,000 for takaful certificates and insurance policies.
The maximum protection for deposit products excludes interest or dividends accrued from the principal amount and is protected separately by PIDM up to RM20,000.

PIDM's mandates state: deposits coverage is RM250,000 per depositor per member bank (includes both principal AND interest/return), and takaful/insurance protection is capped at RM500,000. Not all products are covered — structured products and NIDs are excluded.

What should be done or concluded based on the scenario?

During a detailed client suitability and investor-protection discussion, a relationship manager must identify the single best answer using the product features, regulatory duty and client-treatment principles in the study text. what is the KEY difference between money market instruments and long-term debt securities?
Long-term debt securities are issued only by governments, while money market instruments are issued only by corporations.
Long-term debt securities pay periodic coupon payments, while money market instruments are discount instruments that do not make periodic payments.
Long-term debt securities are traded in the money market, while money market instruments are traded in the exchange.
Based on the current practice, money market instruments always offer higher returns than long-term debt securities.

The textbook distinguishes: money market instruments are typically discount instruments (issued below par, no periodic payments); long-term debt securities pay periodic coupon payments plus principal at maturity. Both government and corporate entities can issue instruments in either market.

Review the statements below.

I. PIDM protects eligible deposits.
II. PIDM supports confidence in the system.
III. PIDM guarantees all structured products.
IV. PIDM sets the OPR.
Statements I and II are correct.

Which answer should be used in the client explanation?

Duration measurement is one of the crucial tools used by bond investors.

What does duration measure in bond investment?
Same as the time to maturity for all bonds.
Credit risk of the bond investment, including the issuer's ability to meet its financial obligations.
Weighted average time to receive all cash flows, and also measures the sensitivities of the bond portfolio to interest rate changes.

The textbook defines duration as '% change in price for a bond given 1% change in yield'. Duration measures both the weighted average time to receive all cash flows AND the sensitivity of the bond price to changes in interest rates (interest rate risk).

What is the most appropriate conclusion?

Select the option or combination that qualifies as a high-net-worth individual as per the Guidelines on Categories of Sophisticated Investors issued by the SC?
An individual with a primary residence worth RM1.5 million and other assets worth RM1.8 million.
An individual with a total investment portfolio in capital market products amounting to RM900,000.
An individual with a Master's Degree in Business Administration and has been working in the Treasury Department of an FI for the past five (5) years.
An individual who jointly with his spouse has a gross annual income of RM350,000.

Option C is treated as the qualifying choice because the professional qualification plus at least five years' relevant financial-market/treasury experience meets the experience-based Sophisticated Investor criterion used in the question. The other options fall short of the stated net-asset, investment-portfolio, or income thresholds.
A depositor has RM450,000 in each of 1 PIDM member bank. Based on a RM250,000 limit per depositor per member bank, what is the total insured deposit amount?
Coverage is capped at RM250,000 per depositor per member bank. Total insured amount = RM250,000 × 1 = RM250,000.
Islamic banking prohibits riba, maisir and gharar.

What should the product or compliance team do?

Select the option or combination that BEST describes the structure of the financial market?
Foreign exchange market transactions are driven only by speculative flows.
Money market deals in both short-term [less than one (1) year] and long-term [more than one (1) year] financial instruments.
Derivatives market is the financial market for derivatives and financial instruments such as futures contracts and options.
Financial products traded in OTC market include swaps, forward rate agreements, and futures contracts.

The textbook defines the derivatives market as 'the financial market for derivatives and financial instruments such as futures contracts or options'. The money market is for short-term instruments only (up to 1 year). FX events have a knock-on effect on other markets. OTC products include swaps and forwards but NOT futures — futures are exchange-traded.

Review the statements below in relation to structured product design and protection considerations.

I. A structure may be designed to reflect a particular market view or underlying exposure.
II. Legal documentation, payout terms, credit exposure, market risk and exit limitations should be understood before investing.
III. Principal protection removes all credit, market and early-exit risks, so no suitability review is required.
IV. A derivative component can never be part of a structured product because derivatives must always be separate products.
I and II only — both statements describe valid structuring uses and protection considerations
I and III only — principal protection removes every relevant risk and suitability concern
II and IV only — documentation matters but derivatives can never form part of the structure
III and IV only — both statements describe a risk-free interpretation of structured products
Statements I and II are correct. Structured products can include derivative components, and principal protection does not remove all risks.

During a detailed client suitability and investor-protection discussion, a relationship manager must identify the single best answer using the product features, regulatory duty and client-treatment principles in the study text. what are the KEY components of a compliance programme that RIs must implement under Section 19 of AMLA?
Key risk management measures of RIs.
Training programmes for employees and senior management.
Internal policies, procedures on employee recruitment and training, and independent audit and control measures.
Customer transaction limits and branch locations.

Section 19 of AMLA requires RIs to implement compliance programmes including 'internal policies, procedures, controls, employee integrity evaluation, ongoing employee training, and independent audit function'. Customer transaction limits or branch locations are operational matters, not core AML compliance programme components.
reducing overall risk when assets are not highly correlated
Combining assets with low correlation can reduce overall portfolio risk.
Under BNM's Guidelines on Product Transparency and Disclosure, what is the KEY requirement that FIs must ensure before selling a new investment-linked insurance product to the customers?
FIs must set up a complaint channel after receiving complaints from customers.
FIs must ensure that customers have prior experience in trading in the stock market.
FIs must provide a minimum guaranteed return on the investment product, as it is an insurance-linked product.
FIs must ensure that the new product is aligned with the customer's risk appetite and financial goals.

Under the Guidelines on Product Transparency and Disclosure, FIs must ensure products are 'aligned with the customer's risk appetite and financial goals' before selling. Setting up complaint channels after sale or requiring stock market experience are not the key pre-sale requirements.

Which option best applies to this situation?

Select the option or combination that BEST describes the money laundering process?
Integration is a process whereby the money from illegal activities is channeled into the financial system.
Layering is a process of placing illegal proceeds into the banking system to disguise the origins of funds.
Placement is a process of creating complex activities of financial transactions designed to disguise the audit trail of the sources of funds.
Money laundering is a process of converting money or property, which is derived from illegal activities, to give it a legitimate appearance.

The textbook defines money laundering as 'the process of converting money or property, which is derived from illegal activities, to give it a legitimate appearance'. Placement is the physical disposal of cash; Layering creates complex transactions to disguise the audit trail; Integration returns laundered funds to the economy as legitimate funds.
Select the option or combination that on Malaysia's dual banking system is TRUE?
There is no major difference between conventional banking and Islamic banking as both operate on interest-free basis.
Similar to a conventional banking overdraft facility, Islamic banking also imposes a commitment fee for its cash-line facility.
In the Islamic banking system, the customer-banker relationship is basically that of debtor-creditor relationship.
In Islamic banking, there is no extra charge for delay or late payments by customers, unlike conventional banking.

The textbook states: 'In Islamic banking, there is no extra charge for any delay or late payment by customers… there are no extra charges in terms of percentage to the total amount due. There is also no commitment fee chargeable for its cash-line facility'. The banker-customer relationship in Islamic banking is not debtor-creditor but a project manager or financier function based on profit or loss-sharing.
A Product Highlights Sheet should describe:
A PHS describes salient features, key risks, fees, charges and other important information.
In an 80-question mock exam, a candidate answers 52 questions correctly. What percentage score did the candidate achieve?
Score percentage = correct answers / total questions × 100 = 52 / 80 × 100 = 65%.

Review the case and choose the best answer.

A bond investor bought a 5-year corporate bond two (2) years ago. The bond was rated as single A by RAM. Recently, RAM has downgraded the bond to BBB due to mismanagement by the current management.

What would be the likely impact on the bond?
Bond price will remain unchanged due to the shorter duration.
Bond investors will be given a choice to convert the bond into company shares due to the downgrading of the rating.
Bond price will fall sharply as the perceived default risk is greater with the rating downgrade.
Bond yield will increase due to high demand for the bond.

The textbook states 'bonds with lower ratings carry higher default risk and trade at lower prices'. A rating downgrade from A to BBB signals increased perceived default risk, causing investors to demand higher yields, which directly reduces bond prices through the inverse price-yield relationship.

Which option avoids the common exam trap?

Maintaining financial and price stability, and promoting safe and efficient payment system in Malaysia is the primary responsibility of:

The textbook states BNM's primary objective is 'to promote monetary stability and financial stability'. BNM also promotes safe and efficient payment systems. The SC regulates capital markets; Labuan FSA regulates the Labuan IBFC; the Ministry of Finance handles fiscal policy.
A new profile has limited information about objectives and risk tolerance. What should be done before any product selection?
Obtain sufficient information for suitability assessment
Sufficient KYC and suitability information should be obtained first.

PIDM administers the deposit insurance system and plays an important role in ensuring stability of the banking system.

Which of the following is a benefit to the financial system due to the deposit insurance provided by PIDM?
PIDM protects member banks from failing by protecting depositors' deposits placed with them.
PIDM complements the existing regulatory framework by providing incentives for the member banks to improve their risk management practices through a differential premium system framework.
PIDM contributes to the profitability of the member banks by charging low premium to insure depositors' deposits placed with member banks.
PIDM promotes public confidence by encouraging the public to place deposits with certain member banks with sound risk management framework.

The textbook states PIDM 'reinforces and complements the existing regulatory and supervisory framework by providing incentives for sound risk management through the Differential Premium System (DPS) framework for member banks'. PIDM protects depositors, not member banks themselves. The DPS charges higher premiums to riskier banks, incentivising better risk management.

Which response best resolves this case?

Select the option or combination that regulations governs the development, marketing, and sales of structured products and ensures investor protection?
Guidelines on Introduction of New Products and Guidelines on Products Highlight Sheet.

The Guidelines on Introduction of New Products (BNM) and Guidelines on Product Highlight Sheet govern the development, marketing, and sales of structured products. AMLA governs AML compliance; Basel III governs capital adequacy; the Personal Data Protection Act governs personal data.

What is the best answer to the client’s question?

When the YTM of a bond increases, what would happen to its price?
Price of the bond remains unchanged.
Price of the bond will increase.
Price of the bond will decrease.
Price of the bond will change depending on the coupon of the bond.

The textbook demonstrates through the price-yield curve that 'when r increases, the bond price decreases'. This inverse relationship is a fundamental bond principle — higher required yield means the present value of future cash flows is lower, reducing the bond price.

Why are discount securities issued below the par value?
To ensure that investors can enjoy capital gains if they hold to maturity.
To ensure investors make a return on the difference between what they paid at the time of purchase and the redemption proceeds at maturity.
The difference at maturity represents the fee earned by the investment bank that facilitated the issuance of the discount instrument.

Discount securities 'are issued at a discount to par value and mature at par value, so the return on the investment is the difference between the purchase price and the par value received at maturity'. This is the mechanism by which investors earn a return without periodic interest payments.

A person with access to account information cannot treat confidentiality as ending merely because the person has left the relevant role. The statutory duty is designed to preserve confidential financial information beyond the period of employment or engagement, unless disclosure falls within a permitted exception. This is the continuing duty of:
FSA secrecy obligations continue after employment or the relevant relationship ends.
Using the approximate Fisher relationship, a nominal interest rate is 5% and inflation is 3%. What is the approximate real interest rate?
Approximate real interest rate = nominal rate − inflation rate = 5% − 3% = 2%.

Review the statements below.

I. KYC supports financial needs analysis.
II. Risk tolerance is relevant to suitability.
III. KYC is required only after a complaint.
IV. Profile information never needs updating.
Statements I and II are correct.
Under the Guidelines on AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs issued by BNM, what should an RI do when a customer refuses to provide information for CDD purposes?
Proceed with the business relationship if the customer is a high valued customer.
Proceed with the business relationship and report to BNM.
Proceed with the business relationship and charge the customer a penalty.
Terminate the business relationship and file an STR with the competent authority.

The textbook states: 'RI should not commence business relationship/perform any transaction or in the case of existing business relationship, it should terminate such business relationship and lodge STR with FIU' when a customer refuses to provide CDD information.

Review the case and choose the best answer.

Customer X purchased a 3-year 100% principal protected structured product based on the upside performance of Nikkei 225 index.

If Customer X were to make an early redemption of the structured product, which of the following is TRUE on the redemption value?
Customer X will receive 100% principal back, plus some profit as determined by the issuer in consultation with the customer at the point of the redemption.
Customer X will receive 100% principal if the option on Nikkei 225 index is in-the-money.
Customer X will receive 100% principal amount only if the market interest rate goes up.
Customer X will receive the sum of proceeds from unwinding the option purchased, plus the prevailing mark to market value of the zero NID.

The textbook states: 'Investors who terminate their investments early very often may not be able to get back all of their initial investments. This is because early redemption is subject to mark-to-market (MTM) valuation.' Early redemption proceeds = proceeds from unwinding the option + prevailing MTM value of the zero NID, which may be more or less than the original investment.
What is one of the requirements under the Guidelines on Investor Protection to become a licensed person involved in selling capital market products in Malaysia?
Have at least 10 years of unrelated work experience.
Hold a general business degree with no specific financial training.
Completed only an introductory financial market seminar.

The Guidelines on Investor Protection require employees conducting permitted capital market activities to meet 'fit and proper' requirements, which include minimum criteria, passing relevant examination modules (such as IPPC), and CPE requirements. Years of unrelated experience or a general business degree alone do not satisfy these requirements.
PIDM administers the deposit insurance system.

What should be done or concluded based on the scenario?

During a detailed client suitability and investor-protection discussion, a relationship manager must identify the single best answer using the product features, regulatory duty and client-treatment principles in the study text. what is the maximum insurance coverage for takaful certificates and insurance policies by PIDM?

The textbook and PIDM mandates confirm the maximum protection for takaful certificates and insurance policies is RM500,000 per policyholder. For deposits, the limit is RM250,000 per depositor per member institution.

Which answer reflects the correct investor-protection outcome?

The SC's Guidelines on AML/CFT/CPF also referenced the FATF standards.

What is the PRIMARY responsibility of RIs with regard to countering PF?
Implement targeted financial sanctions without delay to disrupt WMD financing.
Impose heavy fines and jail terms on RIs dealing with sanctioned entities on WMD financing.
RIs are banned from all transactions with non-FATF member countries.
RIs are required to make enhanced reporting only for transactions above USD50,000 equivalent.

The FATF standards require countries to 'implement targeted financial sanctions without delay to enable prevention, suppression and disruption of the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction'. RIs must implement these sanctions without delay — not impose their own fines, ban all transactions, or set thresholds.

A private equity firm wants to offer shares in FCY to a group of accredited investors. One of the investors is a trust company licensed by the Labuan FSA.

Can this investor qualify as an accredited Investor?
No, because the investor must self-declare net assets of more than RM10 million or in FCY equivalent.
No, because the offering is in FCY, not Ringgit.
Yes, only if the offering is Shariah-compliant.
Yes, because the trust company is a licensed entity registered with Labuan FSA.

The textbook lists 'trust companies licensed by the Labuan FSA' as qualifying accredited investors under the SC's Sophisticated Investors Guidelines. A licensed entity from Labuan FSA qualifies regardless of currency of offering.
A bond is priced at RM100 and has modified duration of 5. If yield rises by 1.00 percentage points, what is the approximate new price using duration approximation?
Approximate % price change = −modified duration × change in yield. = −5 × 1.00% = -5.00%. New price ≈ RM100 × (1 -0.0500) = RM95.

The Guidelines on Investor Protection is jointly issued by BNM and the SC to promote market confidence and ensure investor protection.

Under these Guidelines:
financial institutions are classified as exempt dealers to carry out permitted capital market activities.
the SC is the relevant authority that may determine the 'fit and proper' criteria pursuant to Section 76 (11) of CMSA.
ERPs are required to seek exemption from either the SC or BNM in order to carry out permitted capital market activities.
both the RPs and ERPs are required to maintain a register of securities, either in physical or electronic form, and be readily available for inspection by BNM.

The Guidelines on Investor Protection state that 'RP and ERPs are required to maintain a register of securities, either in physical or electronic format, and be readily available for inspection upon request from BNM'. Under Section 76(11) of CMSA, BNM (not the SC) is the relevant authority that determines 'fit and proper' criteria for ERPs.

An investment bank sells a 3-year 100% principal protected structured product based on a bearish view on the price of gold.

What would the dealer in the investment bank do to structure this product?
Do nothing but monitor the market every day to decide on the next course of action.
Buy a 3-year zero NID and buy a put option on the price of gold.
Buy a 3-year zero NID and buy a call option on the price of gold.
Buy a 3-year zero coupon and sell a put option on the structured product to the customer.

For a bearish view on gold, the dealer buys a put option (which profits when gold falls). Combined with a zero-coupon NID for principal protection, the structure is: buy ZNID + buy put option on gold. A call option would benefit from a bullish (rising) gold view.
Select the option or combination that on the 'moneyness' of options is CORRECT?
A put option is out-of-the-money if the price of the underlying asset is below the exercise price of the option.
A put option is in-the-money if the price of the underlying is equal to the exercise price of the option.
A call option is in-the-money if the price of the underlying asset is above the exercise price of the option.
A call option is out-of-the-money if the price of the underlying asset is equal to the exercise price of the option.

The textbook's moneyness table confirms: 'A call option is in-the-money (ITM) when spot price > strike price'. A put option is OTM when spot > strike (not below). At-the-money is when spot = strike for both. A call option is OTM when spot < strike.
Layering in money laundering is mainly used to:
Layering uses transactions to disguise the trail and origin of illicit funds.

Lucy is a retiree who depends on her savings to meet her monthly expenditures. Lucy approaches Alex, a Relationship Manager from a financial institution to help her structure a suitable investment portfolio to meet her financial needs.

What type of investment portfolio should Alex recommend to Lucy?
A portfolio of short-term money market instruments that provides a steady stream of regular income to meet her financial needs.
A non-principal protected structured product with gold as an underlying asset as gold price is expected to increase over time.
A 15-year investment linked insurance product to ensure her future financial needs.
A mix of high dividend stocks and long-term corporate bonds to enhance returns to meet her future needs.

KYC and suitability assessment requires matching the product to the client's needs. A retiree depending on savings needs capital preservation and regular income — a short-term money market portfolio is most appropriate. Long-term or high-risk products (15-year insurance, gold-linked structured product, equities) are unsuitable.

Review the statements below in relation to fair conduct and ethical sales practice.

I. Sales staff should avoid misrepresentation, concealment of material facts and pressure-selling.
II. Relevant features, risks, fees, restrictions and disclaimers should be disclosed before the decision is made.
III. Switching solely to create new commission is acceptable where no benefit exists, as long as a form is signed.
IV. Unverified rumours may be used to discredit alternatives when the in-house product appears stronger.
I and II only — both statements reflect fair conduct, objective disclosure and ethical sales practice
I and III only — signed forms make commission-driven switching acceptable
II and IV only — disclosure matters and rumours are acceptable competitive tools
III and IV only — both statements describe valid ways to increase sales volume
Statements I and II are correct. Churning and unfair competitive practices are inconsistent with fair conduct.

In June 2021, Bank A issued a 10-year 6% sub-debt maturing in June 2031 with an embedded option to call back at par after three (3) years. In 2025, the market interest rate dropped to 4.5%.

Which of the following is the MOST likely action by Bank A and the impact on the investors?
Sub-debt will automatically be converted into Bank A's equity shares.
Bank A will exercise the call on the bond (redeem) at par, thus investors will face reinvestment risk.
Coupon rate will reset at 4.5% for the remaining maturity if Bank A does not exercise the call option.
Investors will be given a choice to put the bond back with Bank A.

When interest rates fall below the bond's coupon rate, the issuer can refinance at a lower cost by calling the bond early. The textbook states: 'If the interest rate drops below the original coupon rate, the issuer is likely to call the bonds.' Bondholders then face reinvestment risk as they must reinvest at the lower prevailing rates.
A deposit protection query involves several financial products. What is the correct response?
Only eligible protected products are covered
Every product from a group is covered
PIDM coverage applies to eligible protected products.

The provisions in CMSA accords the SC greater power for the protection of consumer interest.

Which of the following is TRUE of such power?
Requires capital market operators to place the application money from investors (in fundraising exercises) in an interbank deposit.
Accords the SC power to take civil and administrative actions on capital market offenders.
Allows the SC to recover five (5) times the amount of losses through civil action for market misconduct, including market manipulation.
Prevents the SC from extending investor protection to clients of financial institutions regulated by BNM.

Under CMSA, the SC has power to take civil and administrative actions on capital market offenders (Section 354). The SC can recover three times (not five times) losses through civil action. The CMSA also extended investor protection to clients of financial institutions regulated by BNM through the Guidelines on Investor Protection.
A zero-coupon component must grow to RM100,000 in 3 years. If the annual yield is 3%, how much should be invested today?
Present value = future value / (1 + yield)^n = RM100,000 / (1 + 3%)^3 = RM91,514.17.

What is the best answer to the client’s question?

Capital market represents one of the components of the financial markets.

Which of the following descriptions on capital market is CORRECT?
Capital market is a market where short-term money market instruments are bought and sold.
Capital market refers to a financial market where new shares and stocks of companies are exclusively issued and traded.
Capital market operates fairly independently, and its activity does not have an impact on the other financial markets.
Capital market is an important avenue for companies and government to raise capital and also provide liquidity to investors to buy and sell securities.

The textbook states the capital market 'is an important avenue for companies and government to raise capital and also provide liquidity to investors to buy and sell securities'. The money market (not capital market) deals in short-term instruments. Capital markets include both equity and debt, not just shares. Financial markets are interconnected and not independent.

Review the statements below.

I. Risks should be disclosed.
II. Rumours should not be used as selling points.

What should the RM conclude?

Market participants play important roles in ensuring the efficient functioning of the financial markets.

Which of the following on the role of the market participants is TRUE?
Regulatory authorities sometimes enter the market to capitalise on market volatility to generate some profits.
Arbitragers capitalise on the price discrepancies across markets due to market imperfection or overreaction to certain events to generate trading profits.
Speculators will enter the market after carefully and thoroughly understanding the financial conditions of the companies they speculate in.
Dealers are employed by financial institutions or corporates to engage in speculative buying and selling of financial instruments in order to make money.

The textbook defines arbitragers as those who 'capitalise on price discrepancies across markets due to market imperfection'. Regulatory authorities occasionally enter the FX market to stabilise the Ringgit, not to make profits. Speculators take positions based on market views, not company fundamentals. Dealers make markets but their primary role is not speculative for the institution.

Under the Guidelines on Investor Protection jointly issued by the SC and BNM, ERPs are required to meet the 'fit and proper' requirements.

Which of the following comply with the 'fit and proper' requirements?

A. Minimum 'fit and proper' criteria / Know-Your-Customer procedures / Pass the relevant examination modules.
B. Pass the relevant examination modules / Conduct Customer Due Diligence / Know-Your-Customer procedures.
C. Minimum 'fit and proper' criteria / Pass the relevant examination modules / Continuing Professional Education requirements.
D. Minimum 'fit and proper' criteria / Pass the relevant examination modules / Conduct Customer Due Diligence.

The 'fit and proper' requirements under the Guidelines on Investor Protection comprise three components: (1) minimum fit and proper criteria, (2) pass the relevant examination modules, and (3) comply with Continuing Professional Education (CPE) requirements. CDD is an AML requirement, not a fit and proper requirement.

Under Section 232 of CMSA, the SC requires FSPs to register a prospectus when dealing in securities.

A prospectus is required:
when issuing, offering, or inviting subscriptions for securities, including new bond offering.
on all marketing materials related to unit trust funds targeting retail investors.
only when the dealing in securities involves private placement with accredited investors.
only when the issuer of securities is a foreign entity.

Under Section 232 of CMSA, a prospectus is required 'when issuing, offering, or inviting subscriptions for securities, including new bond offerings'. This applies to public securities issuances. Private placements to accredited investors are exempted under Schedule 6 or 7 of the CMSA.

Review the statements below.

I. A recommendation must have a reasonable basis.
II. False or misleading information can create liability.
III. Priority is never given to orders.
IV. CMSA only covers currency printing.
Statements I and II are correct.

During a detailed client suitability and investor-protection discussion, a relationship manager must identify the single best answer using the product features, regulatory duty and client-treatment principles in the study text. how does PIDM contribute to the stability of the financial system?
By directly lending money to the failing member banks.
By reimbursing depositors promptly should a member bank fail.
By performing an audit on member banks to ensure they operate efficiently.
By regulating interest rates, member banks charge on their loans and deposits.

PIDM 'contributes to the stability of the financial system by dealing with member institution failures expeditiously and reimbursing depositors as soon as possible'. PIDM does not lend to failing banks, perform audits, or regulate interest rates — these are BNM functions.

What is the most appropriate conclusion?

Labuan FSA is a statutory body responsible for the development and administration of the Labuan international business and financial centre.

Which of the following on Labuan FSA is TRUE?
Set up to develop Labuan as an international financial centre to compete with domestic financial market businesses.
Act as the central regulatory, supervisory, and enforcement authority of the international business and financial services.
Allows international businesses to carry out financial transactions in any currencies, including Ringgit.
Comes under the direct supervision of BNM as the nature of business is financial-related.

The textbook states Labuan FSA 'acts as the central regulatory, supervisory, and enforcement authority of the international business and financial services industry in Labuan'. It was set up to develop Labuan as an international, not domestic, financial centre. International businesses may transact in any currency EXCEPT Ringgit. Labuan FSA is independent, not under BNM.

Which option avoids the common exam trap?

Select the option or combination that is TRUE on formulating policies and procedures in the development and marketing of new products by financial institutions under the Guidelines on Introduction of New Products issued by BNM?
Policies and procedures should aim at safeguarding the financial institutions from liability under applicable anti-fraud and fair practice laws and regulations.
Policies and procedures should be approved by the head of sales in consultation with the head of product owner.
Policies and procedures should ensure that the financial institutions maximise the sales of high-revenue-generating products, as the development cost of new products is high.
Policies and procedures should incorporate provisions to restrict the freedom of choice given to customers to ensure maximum sales.

The Guidelines on Introduction of New Products requires policies to 'safeguard financial institutions from liability under applicable anti-fraud and fair practice laws'. Policies should protect investors and ensure fair practices — not maximise sales or restrict customer choice. Policies must be approved by appropriate governance structures, not just the head of sales.
The market that supports short-term funding and liquidity is the:
The money market supports short-term borrowing, lending and liquidity.

Which of the following are scenarios whereby disclosures may be permitted under Section 134 (Permitted Disclosures) of FSA?

Review the claims below. Which combination is correct?

I. Information or document has been lawfully made available to the public.
II. Customer's personal representative has consented to the disclosure in writing.
III. Customer's accountant has verbally consented to the disclosure.
IV. Customer has accepted the bank's letter of offer which includes a clause permitting the disclosure.

Under Section 134 permitted disclosures: (I) information lawfully made available to the public; and (IV) customer's acceptance of letter of offer with a disclosure consent clause. A personal representative must give WRITTEN consent (not verbal). A customer's accountant's verbal consent does not satisfy the requirement.

For a complex unlisted capital market product, a short summary document should not merely highlight attractive benefits. It should support informed decision-making by presenting salient information in a clear and concise manner, including key features, key risks, fees, charges, exit-related information and contact points for enquiries or complaints. This document is the:
A Product Highlights Sheet contains clear and concise information on salient product features, key risks, fees, charges and other important information.
A discount security is bought for RM95,000 and redeemed at RM100,000 after 180 days. Using a 365-day year, what is the approximate annualised yield?
Annualised yield ≈ (redemption value − purchase price) / purchase price × 365 / days. = (RM100,000 − RM95,000) / RM95,000 × 365 / 180 = 10.67%.
A bond is best described as:
a debt obligation of an issuing entity
Bonds are debt securities issued to raise funds.

During an exam-style client discussion, a relationship manager is asked to identify the most accurate regulatory or product-treatment statement before making any recommendation. a Risk Disclosure Statement must be provided to potential investors who are interested in investing in structured products in order for them to:

From an investor-protection perspective, which statements are true?

I. read and understand the risks involved.
II. keep for future reference and record-keeping.
III. determine the suitability of the investment based on their risk tolerance.
IV. make an informed investment decision.

The textbook confirms investors must receive a Risk Disclosure Statement so they can: (I) read and understand risks, (II) keep it for future reference, (III) determine suitability based on risk tolerance, and (IV) make informed decisions. All four purposes (I, II, III, IV) are valid.

Which one of the following describes the expectations on financial service providers under the Guidelines on Product Transparency and Disclosures?

Which combination gives the best answer?

I. Allowing sales of products to the market prior to adequate systems monitoring and controls, as long as approved by the Board.
II. Products approved by internal Shariah controls are exempted from these Guidelines.
III. Publicly making available Product Disclosure Sheets for all products on the website.
IV. Good business conduct practices, such as disclosure standards in business culture, and supported by the Board and Senior Management.

Statement IV is true. The Guidelines on Product Transparency and Disclosures require 'good business conduct practices, including disclosure standards, supported by the Board and Senior Management'. Products should NOT be sold before adequate systems are in place; all products including Shariah-approved ones are subject to these Guidelines; making PDS available only online is insufficient.

During an exam-style client discussion, a relationship manager is asked to identify the most accurate regulatory or product-treatment statement before making any recommendation. which of the following events or actions would cause interest rates to rise?

Which statements should remain in the client explanation?

I. The government increases borrowing to fund the increase in fiscal deficit.
II. A decrease in liquidity (supply of funds) in the global financial markets.
III. Inflation is expected to decrease moving forward.
IV. Economic activity is expected to increase with more capital investments being projected.

Interest rates rise when: (I) government increases borrowing (more demand for funds); (II) global liquidity decreases (less supply of funds); and (IV) economic activity increases (higher capital demand). Falling inflation (III) would REDUCE rates, not increase them.
A primary market is mainly used for:
Primary markets are used for new securities issuance.

Which one of the following actions by the salesperson conforms to the best market practices when marketing products to the clients?

Assess the statements below and select the correct combination.

I. Salesperson W discredits other competitors' products in order to highlight the attractiveness of his/her own product.
II. Salesperson X explains the difference of the product features of the two (2) products to the clients and guarantees that his/her product will generate higher returns than his/her competitor.
III. Salesperson Y explains the different risk return analysis of the two (2) products and leave the final investment decision to the clients.
IV. Salesperson Z explains the attractiveness of his/her product using information that he/she claimed to be non-public information to convince the clients to purchase.

Statement III is true. The textbook and Guidelines require licensed persons to explain risk-return trade-offs and leave investment decisions to the client. Salesperson Y explains the 'different risk return analysis of the two products and leaves the final investment decision to the clients' — this is best practice. Discrediting competitors, guaranteeing returns, and using non-public information are all prohibited.

During an exam-style client discussion, a relationship manager is asked to identify the most accurate regulatory or product-treatment statement before making any recommendation. which of the following are components of the Malaysian financial system?

Which set of statements should the RM accept as accurate?

I. Foreign exchange market
II. Capital market
III. Derivative market
IV. Reinsurance market

The textbook lists the components of the Malaysian financial system as: foreign exchange market, money market, equity capital market, debt capital market, commodities market, and derivatives market. I, II, and III are all components. Reinsurance market (IV) is not listed as a component of the financial system in the textbook.

During an exam-style client discussion, a relationship manager is asked to identify the most accurate regulatory or product-treatment statement before making any recommendation. which of the following regulatory relationships on market structure are TRUE?

Review the claims below. Which combination is correct?

I. Money and foreign exchange brokers are regulated by BNM.
II. Commodity futures are regulated by the Securities Commission.
III. Asset management companies are regulated by BNM.
IV. Money lenders are regulated by Kementerian Perumahan dan Kerajaan Tempatan.

The textbook confirms: (I) money and FX brokers are regulated by BNM; (II) commodity futures are regulated by the SC; and (IV) money lenders are regulated by the Ministry of Housing and Local Government (Kementerian Perumahan dan Kerajaan Tempatan). Asset management companies (III) are regulated by the SC, not BNM.
An investor converts USD50,000 into Ringgit at an exchange rate of RM4.50 per USD. How many Ringgit will the investor receive before charges?
Ringgit received = USD amount × exchange rate = USD50,000 × RM4.50 = RM225,000.

Which of the following on principal guaranteed structured products are TRUE?

I. Involves a guarantor such as a financial institution.
II. No risk of default is involved since it is principal guaranteed.
III. Guarantee is dependent on the financial strength of the guarantor.
IV. No additional cost to provide guarantee.

For principal GUARANTEED structured products, a guarantor (such as a financial institution) is involved (I), and the guarantee's value depends on the financial strength of that guarantor (III). Statement II is false — default risk of the guarantor still exists. Statement IV is false — there is always a cost (premium) to provide a guarantee.

Which one of the following on a callable bond is TRUE?

I. The issuer is likely to call the bond when prevailing interest rates are higher than the coupon rate.
II. Bonds are usually issued at a discount.
III. The price of a callable bond equals the price of an option-free bond plus the price of the call option.
IV. The yield of a callable bond is normally higher than the yield of a straight bond with the same maturity, coupon rate and issuer.

Only the statement that a callable bond normally offers a higher yield than an otherwise identical straight bond is correct. The issuer is likely to call when prevailing rates fall below the coupon rate, and the callable bond value is the option-free bond value minus the value of the issuer's call option.

Which of the following are examples of the implementation of fiscal policies?

From an investor-protection perspective, which statements are true?

I. Reduction of policy rates to stimulate the economy.
II. Increase in government spending on infrastructure projects.
III. Provide tax relief to small and medium enterprises.
IV. Purchase of government bonds by the Central Bank.

Fiscal policy involves government spending and taxation decisions. Increase in government spending on infrastructure (II) and providing tax relief to SMEs (III) are fiscal policy measures. Reduction of policy rates (I) is MONETARY policy by BNM. Purchase of government bonds by the Central Bank (IV) is also monetary policy (open market operations).

Review the statements below.

I. PIDM administers deposit insurance.
II. PIDM helps support confidence.

During an exam-style client discussion, a relationship manager is asked to identify the most accurate regulatory or product-treatment statement before making any recommendation. which of the following investors' considerations can be incorporated into the design of a structured product?

Which statements should remain in the client explanation?

I. Investors with a bearish market view.
II. Investors who prefer exposure to a specific asset class and a specific currency.
III. Investors who wish to have no risk exposure for both principal and return components.
IV. Investors who have a short-term horizon for investment.

Structured products can accommodate investors with bearish views (I) through put options, exposure to specific asset classes and currencies (II), and short-term horizons (IV). Statement III is not achievable — it is impossible to have zero risk on both principal AND returns simultaneously; that contradicts the risk-return trade-off principle.

Review the statements below in relation to anti-money laundering controls and customer due diligence expectations.

I. Customer due diligence is required when establishing a business relationship.
II. Enhanced due diligence may be relevant where risk factors indicate higher risk.
III. Incomplete beneficial ownership information can be ignored whenever a relationship appears commercially valuable.
IV. Layering is the final stage where illicit funds are enjoyed after they have already been fully absorbed into the economy.
I and II only — both statements reflect core due diligence and risk-based control expectations
I and III only — commercial value can replace verification where the relationship is important
II and IV only — layering is the final enjoyment stage after funds are absorbed
III and IV only — both statements support simplified treatment for higher-value relationships
Statements I and II are correct. Commercial value does not remove due diligence duties, and layering disguises the trail of funds.

Which one of the following scenarios may result in non-compliance with Section 134 (Permitted Disclosures) of FSA?

Assess the statements below and select the correct combination.

I. Disclosure of customer information as approved by the Senior Management of a financial institution.
II. Disclosure of customer information in compliance with a court order.
III. Disclosure of customer information for criminal or civil proceedings.
IV. A customer gives permission to disclose their information in writing.

Statement I is true. Under Section 134, permitted disclosures include: court orders, legal proceedings, BNM written requests, and customer's written consent. Disclosure 'approved by Senior Management of a financial institution' is NOT a permitted disclosure under Section 134 — internal management approval does not override the statutory secrecy obligation.

Review the statements below.

I. Bonds are debt obligations.
II. Sukuk are Islamic securities.
III. Bonds always remove default risk.
IV. Debt securities are ordinary shares.
Statements I and II are correct.

Which one of the following CORRECTLY describes payments under the Bank Negara Malaysia's Foreign Exchange Administration Rules?

Review the claims below. Which combination is correct?

I. Payment in foreign currency between residents for settlement of trade.
II. Payment in foreign currency between residents and non-resident for settlement of derivatives referenced to Ringgit.
III. Payment in Ringgit between non-residents for settlement of Commodity Murabahah transactions.
IV. Payment in Ringgit between non-residents who are immediate family members for purchase of land only.

Statement III is true. Under BNM's FEA rules, payment in Ringgit between non-residents for settlement of Commodity Murabahah transactions is permitted. FX transactions between residents must use licensed intermediaries. Ringgit-settled derivatives referenced to Ringgit exchange rates between residents and non-residents face restrictions.
A portfolio is worth RM800,000. The target allocation to bonds is 40%. How much should be allocated to bonds?
Allocation amount = portfolio value × target weight = RM800,000 × 40% = RM320,000.

Which of the following on interest rates and bond prices is TRUE?

I. They have an inverse relationship.
II. They move in the same direction at all times.
III. They move in the same direction and also opposite directions at times.
IV. They have no relationship with zero coupon bond.

Statement I is true. The textbook states: 'The price-yield relationship for bonds is an inverse relationship. When the required yield increases, bond price decreases.' This applies to all bonds including zero coupon bonds, whose price is entirely determined by the discount factor applied to their single future cash flow.
The regulator responsible for Malaysia’s capital market is:
The SC regulates Malaysia’s capital market.

Select the option that on the early termination of principal protected structured investment is TRUE?

The early termination price and proceeds will be:
based on the prevailing market price.
based on 100% of the principal regardless of market price.
determined by an arbitration committee established by the investor.

The textbook states: 'Early redemption of structured products is subject to mark-to-market (MTM) valuation, which is at the prevailing bid price.' Therefore, early termination proceeds are based on prevailing market price, which may be more or less than the original principal.

The appointment of a Shariah advisor is required when an issuer wishes to issue, offer or make an invitation for subscription to, or purchase of a Ringgit sukuk. Which of the following entities can be appointed as a Shariah advisor?

Which combination gives the best answer?

I. An Islamic bank approved by BNM to carry out the Islamic Banking Scheme.
II. Majlis Agama Islam Wilayah Persekutuan.
III. Registered Shariah advisors under the Registration of Shariah Advisors Guidelines.
IV. Shariah Advisory Council of BNM.

Under the Guidelines on Unlisted Capital Market Products (Lodge and Launch Framework), eligible Shariah advisors include: (I) Islamic banks approved by BNM; and (III) registered Shariah advisors under the SC's Registration of Shariah Advisors Guidelines. Majlis Agama Islam and BNM's Shariah Advisory Council are not on the eligible list for individual sukuk issuance appointments.

What are the two (2) MAIN building blocks of a principal protected structured investment?

Which statements should remain in the client explanation?

I. Zero Coupon Negotiable Instrument of Deposit
II. Guaranteed coupon component
III. Derivative/option component
IV. An equity component

The textbook states: 'Principal protected structured products are generally structured with a combination of Zero-coupon Negotiable Instrument of Deposits (ZNID) with options.' The two main building blocks are: (I) ZNID — for principal protection; and (III) Derivative/option component — for potential upside returns.
A principal-protected structured investment commonly combines a protection component with:
Principal-protected structures commonly combine protection and derivative components.

Which one of the following describes fair treatment of customers in relation to BNM's Guidelines on Introduction of New Products?

Assess the statements below and select the correct combination.

I. Policies and procedures regarding product offerings and sales activities should be approved by the Chief Executive Officer of the bank to avoid mis-selling and unfair terms to customers.
II. Compensation for sales staff should create a bias towards offering high-revenue product recommendations to the customers.
III. Business practices that restrict customers' freedom of choice should not be implemented.
IV. Customer complaints are addressed only after the customer writes a formal complaint.

Statement III is true. The Guidelines on Introduction of New Products require that 'business practices that restrict customers' freedom of choice should not be implemented'. Policies must ensure fair treatment and freedom of choice. CEO approval of all sales activities is not a specific requirement. Compensation structures should not create bias toward high-revenue products.

Money launderers use different techniques to launder illicit funds. One technique used is that the funds are shuttled through a web of multiple bank accounts to disguise their origin.

Which one of the following definitions describes the above-mentioned activity?

The textbook defines 'Layering' as 'separating illicit proceeds from their source by creating complex layers of financial transactions designed to disguise the audit trail and provide anonymity'. Shuttling funds through multiple bank accounts to disguise origin is textbook layering.
A bond has a par value of RM3,000, an annual coupon rate of 3%, and is trading at RM2,940. What is its current yield?
Current yield = annual coupon / market price. Annual coupon = 3% × RM3,000 = RM90. Current yield = RM90 / RM2,940 = 3.06%.
Islamic banking prohibits riba, maisir and gharar.

Which of the following on a callable bond is TRUE?

I. The issuer is likely to call the bond when prevailing interest rates are higher than the coupon rate.
II. The bond is usually issued at a discount.
III. The yield of a callable bond is normally higher than the yield of a straight bond with the same maturity, coupon rate and issuer.
IV. The price of a callable bond equals the price of an option-free bond plus price of the call option.

Only the statement that a callable bond normally offers a higher yield than an otherwise identical straight bond is correct. The issuer is likely to call when prevailing rates fall below the coupon rate, and the callable bond value is the option-free bond value minus the value of the issuer's call option.

A product recommendation made purely because of sales targets, without practical steps to understand objectives, financial situation and particular needs, creates a capital market conduct concern. Section 92 requires a reasonable basis for recommendations.

Under the Guidelines on Investor Protection, what are the standards for 'fit and proper'?

From an investor-protection perspective, which statements are true?

I. Comply with the minimum 'fit and proper' criteria.
II. Comply with the Continuing Professional Education requirements.
III. Meet relevant examination requirements.
IV. Hold a Capital Markets Services Representative's Licence.

The 'fit and proper' standards under the Guidelines on Investor Protection include: (I) minimum fit and proper criteria, (II) CPE requirements, and (III) passing relevant examination modules. Holding a Capital Markets Services Representative's Licence (IV) is a consequence of meeting these requirements, not one of the three standards itself.

Ignore the issue for large amounts

A Development Financial Institution regulated by Bank Negara Malaysia.
Gizmo Sdn. Bhd. which issues a PDS that does not come with any form of guarantees.

An investor approached your bank to structure a suitable structured product for his investment needs. What information is required from the investor?

I. Investor's goal.
II. Investor's risk appetite.
III. Investor's time horizon.
IV. Investor's preference of underlying instruments.

To structure a suitable structured product, the textbook states advisors must understand: the investor's goal, risk appetite, time horizon, AND preference of underlying instruments. All four pieces of information (I, II, III, IV) are required for a comprehensive suitability assessment.

Which of the following on structured products is TRUE?

Assess the statements below and select the correct combination.

I. Equity indices are more representative and less volatile compared to a single stock.
II. Investors need not worry about default risk when buying structured products from a financial institution.
III. Investors need not worry about liquidity risk when investing in structured products.
IV. Legal documentations are not crucial for a structured product investment which is maturing in a month.

Statement I is true. The textbook states: 'Equity indices are more representative and less volatile compared to a single stock.' Investors DO face default risk (issuer credit risk) and liquidity risk when investing in structured products. Legal documentation is always required regardless of maturity.

I. Primary markets are for new issues.

A principal-protected structured product invests RM200,000 and gives 70% participation in a 8% rise of the underlying asset. Ignoring fees and taxes, what amount is payable at maturity?
Payoff = principal + principal × underlying return × participation. = RM200,000 + RM200,000 × 8% × 70% = RM211,200.

Which of the following describes portfolio diversification?

The following points are raised during the discussion. Which are accurate?

I. Combining assets with a low correlation will lower the overall risk of the portfolio.
II. Reduced loss but increased volatility during times of market uncertainties.
III. Portfolio review should be performed regularly to know portfolio performance.
IV. A simplified sales process is conducted when rebalancing portfolio compared with a new portfolio.

Portfolio diversification benefits include: (I) combining assets with low correlation lowers overall portfolio risk; and (III) regular portfolio review ensures performance monitoring. Statement II is incorrect — diversification reduces volatility, not increases it. Statement IV is incorrect — rebalancing a portfolio is just as complex as building a new one.

A RM1 million par value bond has a 7% annual coupon and is priced at RM950,000 with 5 years to maturity.  Using the approximate YTM formula, which of the following is closest to the yield to maturity?  [Approximate YTM ≈ (Annual Coupon + (Par − Price)/n) / ((Par + Price)/2)]

Annual Coupon = 7% × RM1,000,000 = RM70,000. Capital gain per year = (RM1,000,000 − RM950,000) / 5 = RM10,000. Numerator = RM70,000 + RM10,000 = RM80,000. Denominator = (RM1,000,000 + RM950,000) / 2 = RM975,000. Approximate YTM = RM80,000 / RM975,000 ≈ 8.2%. Since the bond trades at a discount, YTM must be ABOVE the coupon rate of 7%, confirming the 8.2% result. Note: 7.0% would mean trading at par.

An investor observes that the Malaysian yield curve has shifted from a normal (upward-sloping) shape to a flat shape. According to yield curve theories, which of the following BEST explains this transition?

Which set of statements should the RM accept as accurate?

I. The Expectations Theory suggests the market now expects short-term rates to remain unchanged or fall, reducing the premium for long-term bonds.
II. The Liquidity Preference Theory suggests investors now prefer longer maturities due to higher long-term yields.
III. The Market Segmentation Theory suggests all investors have simultaneously moved from short-term to long-term investments.
IV. The Expectations Theory suggests the market expects inflation to rise sharply, flattening the curve.

Statement I is true. The Expectations Theory states that long-term rates equal the average of expected future short-term rates. Which of the following correctly identifies derivatives that are forward COMMITMENTS (both parties obligated) vs. contingent CLAIMS (right but not obligation)? Forward Commitments: [X] Contingent Claims: [Y]

A RM1 million par value zero coupon bond is issued with a 5-year maturity. An investor requires a return of 6% per annum.  What price should the investor pay for this bond?

An investor buys a call option on Bursa Malaysia equity futures with a strike price of 1,600 points. The current index level is 1,550 points. The option premium is 25 points.  What is the intrinsic value and time value of this option?

Intrinsic value = 25 points; Time value = 0 points

A call option is in-the-money only when spot price > strike price. Here, spot (1,550) < strike (1,600), so the call is out-of-the-money. Intrinsic value for an OTM option = 0, because intrinsic value cannot be negative. Option premium = intrinsic value + time value, so 25 = 0 + time value. Therefore, the time value is 25 points.
